newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up sharply, stock hike absorbed.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up sharply, stock hike absorbed.

text.p: COMEX copper defied Tuesday's large hike in LME stocks to end sharply higher as traders said the market had already discounted the build-up of metal as a much anticipated but delayed "one-off" event in Asia.
LME stocks rose 11,475 tonnes to 134,700 tonnes with much of the net gains in Singapore.
"The stock increase in Singapore has been expected for weeks," Mike Frawley of Dean Witter Reynolds said.
A total hike of about 30,000 tonnes was expected at the warehouse in the island-state and a further 10,000 tonnes could be added, Frawley said.

"It's discounted, it's in the market. The bigger issue is that physical business is still quite good and there is a lot of very aggressive shortcovering, and we are looking for LME cash to threes to widen considerably," Frawley added.
March COMEX settled 3.60 cents firmer at 105.15 cents per pound - its highest since last June - traded 105.55 to 101.00 cents. Spot January went out 4.20 cents up at 108.20 cents.
Volume was good at an estimated 16,000 lots versus Monday's official 4,579 lots.
The LME cash to three months premium widened slightly Tuesday to $125/$135.
COMEX stocks Tuesday rose 368 short tons to 29,920 short tons.
